title: Ultrasound-Based Assessment of Lumbosacral Junction Mobility: Reliability, Concurrent Validity with Radiography, and Mobility Characteristics in Sway-Back Posture
content: Background/Objectives: Sway-back posture (SBP) is a common postural deviation associated with low back pain; however, segmental mobility at the lumbosacral junction is poorly understood. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate the reliability of ultrasound (US)-based L5/S1 angular mobility measurements, their association with radiographic measurements, and mobility characteristics in individuals with SBP. Methods: This two-part cross-sectional study assessed intra- and inter-rater reliability of US-based L5/S1 angle measurements in 12 healthy adults and associations with radiographic measurements in 18 participants with low back pain (Study 1). Study 2 compared L5/S1 mobility between typical sagittal spinal alignment (TSA) and SBP groups in a sample of 96 healthy adults. Results: US-based measurements yielded favorable reliability point estimates for intra-rater (ICC = 0.93–0.98) and inter-rater (ICC = 0.85–0.98) assessments. US-derived L5/S1 flexion and extension ROM correlated strongly with radiographic measurements (r = 0.78–0.94). L5/S1 extension ROM was significantly greater in the SBP group than in the TSA group (4.30 ± 2.66° vs. 2.40 ± 1.53°; p = 0.029). Between-group differences in L5/S1 flexion ROM and overall thoracolumbar mobility were not statistically significant. Conclusions: The strong association between US-derived L5/S1 ROM and radiographic measurements provides preliminary support for the validity of this non-invasive method. Greater L5/S1 extension mobility may characterize SBP, highlighting the potential value of segment-specific mobility assessment alongside conventional measures of overall lumbar mobility.
